units.translation: And upon his heart ran a saffron-dyed drop
pouring to the ground the dye of saffron
the city then called Cronia, but now Hierapolis, as Isigonus and Aeschylus (fr. 10) in the Aetna (i.e. the Aetnaeae) record.
the city then called Cronia, but now Hierapolis, as Isigonus and Aeschylus
wishing to cast Cronus from his throne
and he himself bound his aged father Cronus
where the river breathes forth its might from its very temples
i.e. the striking of weapons hurled against the shield.
meeting with the dense clatter beneath the city
and with a din it resounds upon my stricken and all-wretched head
Was this then a secret gift from Orestes?
some evil cold falls upon my heart
the guileful punishment of a secret battle

in a corrupt passage, in M it is κρυπτά [hidden things] or κρυπτάν [hidden], but the scholiast explains κρυπτά [hidden things] above the verse with the words τὰ κρυπτὰ φανερώσει [he will reveal the hidden things], and in the margin θέλων πολλὰ κρυπτὰ εὑρίσκει [wishing he finds many hidden things].
καὶ κρυπτά [and hidden things] is corrupt for κἄκρυπτα [and not hidden]: see under ἄκρυπτος [not hidden].
for in a messenger a hidden word is set upright
and many other hidden things he will reveal, needing them
τὰ κρυπτὰ φανερώσει [he will reveal the hidden things]
θέλων πολλὰ κρυπτὰ εὑρίσκει [wishing he finds many hidden things]
to conceal with accusative of person and thing
and he hid those who had enmity
do not hide from me this which I am about to suffer
and beneath the earth hidden benefits for mortals
they brought forth libations more ready than laughter, pouring (thus Dobraeus for χαίρουσα [rejoicing]) a much-weeping lament, hidden
it was not hidden, but it shines, a terribly bright light, the harm
having found some escape secretly with ships
nor leave pitchers, neither wine-jars nor water-jars, in wealthy houses
κέκτημαι [I have acquired] or ἔκτημαι [I have acquired] I have acquired for myself, I possess
ὁ κεκτημένος [the one who has acquired] the owner
you acquired great wealth for your children with the spear
and he acquired the people of the Lydians and Phrygians
such a thing would a thievish man acquire
and he will acquire without the spear both himself and the land
common is fortune, but the judgment belongs to the owners
and even dead he will acquire pollution
who would buy friends, the owners?
ὁ κεκτημένος [the one who has acquired]
and that they once obtained possessions by lot through the iron-wielding hand
they divided by lot with the hammered Scythian iron the whole property of possessions
